title: Read Errors First: Save Troubleshooting Time

scenes.line1: Ever wasted time running random tools?
scenes.say: Have you ever spent ages running random commands and still missed the root cause? What should you actually do first?

scenes.label: Layer
scenes.sub: The error message tells you which layer failed.
scenes.say: The error message almost always points to the exact layer that failed. That's your first clue.
Here are some common errors. Each one tells you exactly where to start looking. For example, 'could not resolve host' means DNS is the problem.
Timeout means something silently dropped your packets. Refused means you reached the host, but nothing's listening. That distinction is huge in interviews.

scenes.question: What’s the first thing to check?
scenes.wrong: Run traceroute or ping right away.
scenes.right: Read the error message—it tells you the layer.
scenes.say: Here's a classic interview trap: Don't jump straight to tools like traceroute or ping. Always read the error message first—it tells you where to start.
